snippet.title: El dinero que no llegaba: el fallo de Chase y Zelle del 16 de noviembre
snippet.description:
El lunes 16 de noviembre de 2026, miles de usuarios en Estados Unidos reportaron problemas con Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank y Zelle. Pero el origen confirmado estaba en un solo banco: JPMorgan Chase atribuyó el problema a un error de software en sus sistemas de hardware locales y dijo que no había evidencia de un ciberataque.

¿Por qué clientes de bancos que funcionaban también esperaban sus pagos? ¿Qué cuentan realmente las cifras de Downdetector? ¿Y qué significa que el dinero siga en la cuenta aunque la transferencia no llegue? Reconstruimos la jornada hora por hora con imágenes reales de noticieros, declaraciones de cada entidad y esquemas en 3D.

CAPÍTULOS
00:00 Una transferencia que no llega
01:46 Nueve de la mañana: los primeros reportes
03:19 Dos de la tarde: el pico (y qué mide Downdetector)
05:06 Cuatro de la tarde: la causa según Chase
06:36 El efecto dominó: cómo un retraso cruza de un banco a otro
08:40 Lo que dijeron los otros bancos y Zelle
10:15 Seis y media de la tarde: la recuperación
11:26 Lo que no sabemos
12:57 No es la primera vez
14:20 Qué hacer si te pasa
15:31 El dinero no desapareció

IMPORTANTE
- Las cifras de Downdetector son reportes de usuarios, no clientes afectados.
- Las escenas en 3D son recreaciones y esquemas genéricos: no muestran instalaciones, redes ni aplicaciones reales de ningún banco. La app «Mi Banco» es ficticia.
- Al 17 de noviembre de 2026, Chase no ha publicado un análisis de causa raíz ni el número de clientes afectados.

FUENTES (consultadas el 16–17 nov 2026)
- NBC News: declaraciones de Chase (comunicado en X, ~4 p. m. ET; «Transactions are now posting normally», ~6:30 p. m. ET), Zelle, U.S. Bank, PNC, Truist, Capital One.
- CBS News: casi 4.800 reportes de Chase hacia las 2 p. m. ET; declaraciones de Bank of America y U.S. Bank; normalidad el martes.
- France 24 / AP / AFP: Joe Evangelisti (JPMorgan Chase), Early Warning Services (Zelle).
- Al Jazeera: dueños de Zelle; Jody Westby (Global Cyber Risk); contexto de Microsoft y la FAA.
- TechTimes (con Barron's, Yahoo Finance, ABC News y Tom's Guide): reportes por banco y por hora; aviso de Wells Fargo.
- American Banker (ago 2026): caída previa de Chase en Zelle; Richard Crone (Crone Consulting).
- FDIC: seguro de depósitos hasta 250.000 dólares por depositante, por banco y por categoría de cuenta.

CRÉDITOS DE IMAGEN
- Video: NBC News, ABC News, WABC-TV (ABC7 Nueva York), WNYW (FOX 5 Nueva York), WKYC Channel 3. Fragmentos breves con crédito en pantalla, con fines informativos.
- Fotos (Wikimedia Commons): «JPMorgan Chase - 270 Park Avenue», ajay_suresh, CC BY 4.0 · «Chase Bank Branch Miami», Phillip Pessar, CC BY 2.0 · «A Chase Bank branch in Knoxville, Tennessee», Harrison Keely, CC BY 4.0 · «Chase ATM», MostlyDross, CC BY 2.0.
- Mapa: us-atlas (U.S. Census Bureau, dominio público).
- Recreación 3D, gráficos y música original: el canal.

*US BANKS, MICROSOFT, AND AVIATION: IS AI TO BLAME OR IS AMERICA'S DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE FAILING?*

*By Milan Sharma*

Millions rely on digital systems to access money, communicate and travel. 

Recent reported disruptions involving major American banks, Microsoft services and aviation infrastructure have raised an uncomfortable question: *how resilient are the systems underpinning everyday life?*

The incidents have different reported circumstances. 

There is no established evidence connecting them to a coordinated cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence.

👉🏽 Has technological efficiency come at the cost of our ability to withstand system failures?

——

*VIDEO HIGHLIGHTS*

* 🔹 Banking customers report access disruptions.
* 🔹 Microsoft failures expose operational vulnerabilities.
* 🔹 Aviation disruptions intensify infrastructure concerns.
* 🔹 Expert warns against excessive digital dependence.

——

01:24 CHAPTER 1: *WHEN BANKING ACCESS FAILS*

Customers reportedly struggled to access online banking services at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and other US institutions. The immediate concern was simple: could people access their money? An inaccessible banking application does not necessarily mean deposits have disappeared.

*“ऑनलाइन मोबाइल बैंकिंग लॉग इनवैलिड हो गए थे जेपी मॉ्गन के। बैलेंस नहीं दिख रहे थे लोगों के।” 01:24*

——

02:14 CHAPTER 2: *THE TECHNOLOGY DEPENDENCY PROBLEM*

Microsoft service disruptions and reported aviation problems added to public anxiety. But separate failures do not establish a shared cause. The real concern is how businesses and public institutions maintain operations when critical technology becomes unavailable.

*“दुनिया भर की कंपनीज में खलबली मच गई।” 02:29*

——

04:56 CHAPTER 3: *IS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RESPONSIBLE?*

The programme raises the possibility of AI involvement. However, the supplied material establishes no forensic evidence linking these outages to autonomous AI activity. Speculation must be distinguished from verified technical findings.

*“इसके पीछे का कारण आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस एआई हो सकता है” 04:56*

——

08:37 CHAPTER 4: *THE EXPERT IDENTIFIES THE REAL RISK*

The technology expert shifts attention from conspiracy theories to infrastructure concentration. Banks, governments and businesses increasingly depend on a limited number of technology providers. One critical failure can affect multiple services.

*“हमने पिछले कुछ सालों में एफिशिएंसी के नाम पर बहुत ज्यादा सेंट्रलाइजेशन कर दिया है।” 08:37*

——

09:20 CHAPTER 5: *THE DANGER IS DEPENDENCY*

The expert’s central argument is about resilience, not machines taking control. Automation has expanded faster than backup arrangements in many organisations. The priority is redundancy, manual alternatives and recovery preparedness.

*“मुझे नहीं लगता एआई कोई मॉन्सर है। मॉन्सर है हमारी डिपेंडेंसी।” 09:20*

snippet.title: BANK OF AMERICA — The $1.2 Billion Admission | Willful AML Violations
snippet.description:
In Charlotte, North Carolina, sits the second-largest bank in America. Three point four trillion dollars in assets. Two hundred eleven thousand people. Three thousand five hundred branches. Fifteen thousand cash machines. It holds America's money. Deposits of more than two trillion dollars. A global systemically important bank. Too big to ignore. This is the story of what it admitted, in writing.

Its watchdog was a computer program called Event Processor. Built in twenty ten. The bank's primary control against dirty money. An alert became a case only at twenty points in thirteen months. That line was set by judgment, and left alone for thirteen years. Below the line, groups produced reports thirty-eight to forty-five percent of the time. A test showed eighteen percent below the line. The repeat called it incorrect.

On the thirteenth of October, three agencies acted in a single morning. FinCEN assessed one point two billion dollars. The bank admitted willful violations. Willful, in civil law, means reckless disregard. Not criminal intent. The OCC added seven hundred fifty million. FinCEN credited it inside its own penalty. Four hundred fifty million to Treasury. Eleven point six six million to OFAC. The total: one point two one billion dollars. The third-largest in Treasury history.

The bank admitted it, in writing. It paid one point two one billion dollars. No one was charged. The senator's question, will anyone be, is still unanswered.

IMPORTANT: The figures must stay apart: $1,211,662,930 total paid is not $1.2bn FinCEN assessment is not $750m OCC (credited INSIDE the $1.2bn, not added) is not $450m payable to FinCEN/Treasury is not $11,662,930 OFAC is not more than $5bn suspicious transactions not timely reported is not more than $1bn national-security/priority illicit-finance risks is not ~$4bn lookback missed SARs (~8,900) is not ~$3.96bn SARs produced from the lookback (more than 8,000) is not $660m+ money orders (680,000+ transactions, ~220,000 groups) is not more than $600m trade-based money laundering indicia is not $700m+ Customer C wires is not $1.7bn Customer A Russia-border wires (around Feb 2022) is not ~$850m wires from Sep 2022 is not $1.1bn UAE-affiliate wires in one quarter (Customer B) is not $250m CFPB 2023 (more than $100m redress + $150m penalties) is not $350m American Express (8 Oct 2026, separate bank) is not $6.9bn Q3 net income is not $0.91 EPS is not $0.17 EPS hit is not $51.39 close (−4.76%) is not $49.26 intraday low is not $3.4tn corporation assets (30 Sep 2026) is not ~$2.7tn BANA assets (FinCEN order's description) is not $30.5bn annual net income is not $434bn TD asset cap is not $3.09bn TD total penalties. "Willful" here is civil-BSA willfulness — reckless disregard or willful blindness — not criminal intent. The $5bn is suspicious transactions the bank failed to report on time, not money proven laundered and not money the bank stole. No criminal charges exist against the bank or any executive; the criminal investigation is demanded, not opened. Customers A, B and C are pseudonyms from the FinCEN order. The 16 November 2026 banking outage was a Chase software bug; Bank of America's systems were operating normally. Figures verified 17 November 2026.

snippet.title: Berkshire Hathaway, the company Warren Buffett built, filed its latest stock holdings on Monday, and
snippet.description:
Berkshire Hathaway, the company Warren Buffett built, filed its latest stock holdings on Monday, and it kept selling banks: about 27 million more Bank of America shares, and a 62% cut to its Capital One stake.

Buffett bought into Bank of America in 2011 with $5 billion when the bank was struggling, and by 2024 Berkshire owned more than a billion shares. Since then it has sold quarter after quarter, and less than half of that stake is left. Berkshire is also sitting on more than $350 billion in cash.

Buffett no longer makes the calls. Greg Abel is CEO and Howard Buffett is chairman. The same day, Buffett gave about $5.5 billion to his family's charities.

The filing doesn't say why. Some see housekeeping after a hugely profitable bet; others see a warning about banks. Crack in the banks, or just cashing out?

snippet.title: Why Zelle Stalled at Other Banks on November 16, 2026
snippet.description:
On November 16, 2026, customers of Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank reported payment problems. According to Chase, the bug was at Chase: a software bug in an on-premise hardware system, which Chase said was not cyber-related. Zelle said its own network was operating normally. Every payment has two ends, and Chase said other banks were affected only when they were a party to a transaction with Chase. Outage reports peaked around 2 p.m. Eastern; by about 6:30 p.m., Chase said transactions were posting normally.

A technical glitch has disrupted online banking services at several major US financial institutions, leaving thousands of customers facing difficulties. Customers of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and other banks reported problems accessing online accounts and completing digital transactions. Banking apps and websites also experienced disruptions. JPMorgan Chase attributed the issue to a technical bug and ruled out a cyberattack. The bank said customer funds remain safe, although some transactions are taking longer than usual.

snippet.title: Why Is Everything Breaking at the Same Time?
snippet.description:
The most dangerous system to go down this week was not an airline or a bank. It was the National Security Agency. Tuesday morning, the National Security Agency (NSA) put its Fort Meade headquarters on a code yellow. By Tuesday night, it was on a code orange, essential personnel only. The agency first called it temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance. Hours later, Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Jay Clayton said the agency had applied a software patch for major vulnerabilities discovered last month, and the patched systems did not come back up as expected. That sequence — alert, reassurance, reversal — is the story of this week. Because the NSA was not alone. In five days, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Microsoft, the banks, United Airlines, and Apple all failed too. I am going to walk through each incident, what was said at the time, and what it means when the systems everyone assumes are redundant keep failing for different technical reasons.

St. Louis Fed Başkanı Alberto Musalem ve Fed üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyonu kontrol altına almak için önümüzdeki dönemde birden fazla faiz artışı gerektiğini belirtti. Waller, Aralık’ta yarım puanlık artış değerlendirilmesini istedi. ECB Başkan Yardımcısı Boris Vujcic de önümüzdeki ay faiz artırımının son derece muhtemel olduğunu, 2027’de başka artışların gelebileceğini söyledi.

Bank of America anketine göre yatırımcıların yapay zeka iyimserliği azaldı, fon yöneticileri teknoloji hisselerindeki ağırlıklarını son 20 yılın en büyük oranında düşürdü. Goldman Sachs ise Fed’in faiz artırımlarının kısa vadede altını baskılayacağını, 2027 sonunda 4.650 dolara, 2028 sonunda ise 5.600 dolara çıkabileceğini öngörüyor.

Nvidia’nın geliri üç aylık dönemde yıllık %103 artışla 115,8 milyar dolara ulaşarak beklentileri aştı. Ekim’de konut satışları yıllık %23,3 geriledi. TÜİK verilerine göre işsizlik %8,1’e, geniş tanımlı işsizlik ise %30,9’a yükseldi.
